question: A robust level of participation and turnout is essential in the European Elections to bolster their democratic legitimacy and ensure a fair representation of the perspectives and values of European voters.

In light of the favourable 2019 turnout, we are interested in strategies that the Commission could implement to promote citizen engagement in elections, with a particular emphasis on measures related to automatic registration in electoral rolls. We believe that numerous first-time voters fail to meet registration deadlines because the public discourse on elections is slow to pick up momentum.

Consequently, even though voters express their intention to vote on election day, they are sometimes unable to do so because they fail to register on time. Our research reveals that 22 out of the 27 Member States have implemented automatic registration on electoral rolls, and this practice is linked to higher voter turnout. What measures could the Commission take to: 1.
Enhance awareness about registration procedures for the forthcoming European elections, taking into account the diverse legal frameworks across Member States?
Facilitate the automatic registration of young voters in Member States where manual registration procedures are in place, so as to ensure their active involvement in the electoral process?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.5.2024) The Commission attaches great importance to support high voter turnout and inclusive participation and is actively supporting Member States’ efforts in this regard.

In December 2023, the Commission adopted a Recommendation on inclusive and resilient elections1, as part of the ‘Defence of Democracy’ package, which encourages Member States to take the necessary steps to facilitate, where applicable, voter and candidate registration in elections, including by providing the necessary information, tools and support at local level.

The use of tools such as online registration should be made easily accessible and user friendly. It also recommends to support young people, especially first time voters, in the exercise of their electoral rights and to address barriers limiting the opportunities of members of different groups to vote and stand as candidate.

The Commission also closely cooperates with the European Parliament on the one-stop-shop for the interinstitutional campaign promoting turnout in the next European elections. The website2 includes detailed ‘How to vote’ pages, which were updated thanks to inputs of the European Cooperation Network on Elections3.

In addition, the Commission provides EU funding of civil society and promotes the recently released ‘Guide to EU citizenship’ made available in December 2023 in the context of the ‘Citizenship Package’.
1 Commission Recommendation (EU) 2023/2829 of 12 December 2023 on inclusive and resilient electoral

processes in the Union and enhancing the European nature and efficient conduct of the elections to the European Parliament. 2 Available at: https://elections.europa.eu/en/ 3 https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/policies/justice-and-fundamental-rights/eu-citizenship-anddemocracy/democracy-and-electoral-rights/european-cooperation-network-elections_en
